records.name: Rome

salary_usd_year.note: Gross annual. EUR: new_grad ~€25,000 (levels.fyi entry-level €24,691-31,935; national Glassdoor Italia junior avg €26,800, with Rome typically a bit below Milan); mid ~€34,000 (Indeed.it Roma blended 'sviluppatore' avg €30,195 as a floor; national mid-level range €35-45k); senior ~€45,000. levels.fyi's Rome senior range (€36,836-94,794, driven by an Uber-linked entry at €238k) shows the same multinational-outlier skew seen in Milan — the high end was excluded from the headline figure.

tehran_travel.note: A direct Iran Air flight FCO-IKA exists (flight IR738, ~4h50m per flight-tracker schedule data), but frequency appears limited/irregular (tracking sites show it not consistently scheduled) — verify the current timetable before booking. The reliable fallback is 1-stop via Istanbul (Turkish Airlines), roughly 9-10h; estimate.

records.tech_scene_note: A smaller but growing tech scene centered on telecom (TIM), IT consulting, and EU/public-sector-adjacent digital work, generally paying somewhat less than Milan.

records.name: Turin

salary_usd_year.note: Gross annual. EUR: new_grad ~€25,500 (Glassdoor Turin software developer 25th percentile €25,525 of 540 submissions, used as junior proxy); mid ~€33,000 (Glassdoor Turin software developer avg €30,100 / software engineer avg €35,000 blended; Indeed/jobted-style blended avg €34,217); senior ~€46,000 (Glassdoor 90th percentile €45,100; levels.fyi senior €47,163-59,153). Turin's sampled tech postings skew toward automotive/embedded-software roles (Stellantis-adjacent) rather than a broad consumer-tech market, and levels.fyi's Turin pages failed to render directly (WebSearch-summarized figures used instead) — treat bands as less certain than Milan/Rome.

tehran_travel.note: No direct flights; connects via Istanbul (Turkish Airlines) or via Milan/Rome first. Estimate based on regional 1-stop itinerary patterns, likely somewhat longer than Milan's routing given Turin's smaller airport and fewer connection options.

records.tech_scene_note: A traditional automotive/industrial engineering city (Stellantis HQ) with a compact tech scene weighted toward embedded systems and automotive software rather than a broad consumer-tech startup culture.

records.name: Madrid

salary_usd_year.note: Gross annual, triangulated from Glassdoor España + KeepCoding (citing Randstad/Jobted) + 10Code (citing LinkedIn Salary/InfoJobs): new_grad €22-30k (used €25k), mid €38-50k for 3-5yr Madrid/Barcelona devs (used €44k), senior — Glassdoor's 'Senior Software Engineer, Madrid' page reports average total comp €59,300 (base €45-63k) and a separate search found median €62k/range €48-77k (used €60k). levels.fyi shows much higher figures (median total comp €53,877 all-levels; entry-level median €29,792) because its self-reporting user base skews toward large multinational/FAANG offices (Google L3-L5 €114-143k, Meta E5 €157-184k) — real but non-representative; Glassdoor's EY junior salary band (€22.7-32.4k) is far more typical of the broad market.

tehran_travel.note: No direct MAD-IKA service; fastest realistic routing is 1-stop via Istanbul (Turkish Airlines) or Doha (Qatar Airways)/Dubai (Emirates), all of which serve Madrid directly; estimate based on general route/schedule knowledge.

records.tech_scene_note: Spain's largest tech hub, home to major multinational offices (Amazon, Google, Meta), deep enterprise/consulting IT presence (Indra, BBVA, Telefonica) and a growing startup scene, but line-level software salaries remain well below Western/Northern Europe.

records.name: Barcelona

salary_usd_year.note: Gross annual, triangulated from Glassdoor España (direct: 'Programador Junior' Barcelona average base ~€21,000 + ~€2,000 supplements ~€23,000/yr total, range €18,950-27,500) + KeepCoding/Randstad city breakdown (€21-27k junior) + 10Code national bands adjusted for Barcelona's ~18% city premium: mid ~€40k (cross-checked against a '3-5yr Madrid/Barcelona developer €38-50k' figure), senior ~€56k (Glassdoor's Barcelona 'Senior Software Engineer' individual listings cluster €60-81k but skew toward 10-14yr veterans, scaled down toward a 6+yr entry-senior band). levels.fyi shows higher figures (median total comp €59,297) again skewed by multinational offices (Microsoft avg €93.7k, N26 up to €198k) — treat as outliers, not typical.

tehran_travel.note: No direct BCN-IKA service; Barcelona-El Prat has confirmed direct flights to Istanbul (Turkish Airlines), Doha (Qatar Airways), Dubai (Emirates), and Abu Dhabi (Etihad) per flightsfrom.com, all of which connect onward to Tehran — the most route options of the three Spanish cities; Istanbul routing is likely fastest; estimate.

records.tech_scene_note: Pay is roughly comparable to Madrid but with a stronger startup/scale-up culture (Glovo, TravelPerk, Factorial) centered on the 22@ innovation district, plus a large international/expat tech workforce.

records.name: Valencia

salary_usd_year.note: Thinner data than Madrid/Barcelona. Triangulated from KeepCoding's city breakdown (junior €18-23k), individual Glassdoor-submitted Valencia salaries for 1-3yr 'Programador' (two data points: €17-19k and €26k), and a blended talent.com/Glassdoor 'Programador' figure spanning all experience levels (median €27,250, 25th pct €22,805, 75th pct €44,750, '1% below national average') used as an anchor for mid/senior since no clean per-level Valencia breakdown exists. Resulting EUR estimates: new_grad €21k, mid €28k, senior €42k. levels.fyi Valencia data (entry-level median ~€19-20k, but 'all levels' median total comp €54,487) looked internally inconsistent and thin-sample, so was not used as the headline figure.

tehran_travel.note: No direct VLC-IKA service; Valencia airport has a confirmed direct Turkish Airlines flight to Istanbul (per flightsfrom.com) which connects onward to Tehran; unlike Madrid/Barcelona, Valencia has no direct Gulf-carrier (Qatar/Emirates/Etihad) service, so Istanbul is the main realistic 1-stop option; estimate.

records.tech_scene_note: A smaller but fast-growing tech scene anchored by local scaleups and an increasing remote-work/digital-nomad community, with noticeably lower software salaries than Madrid or Barcelona offset by a lower cost of living.
